title: AI chip stocks wobble even as investors get clarity on a key OpenAI issue
source_used: Investing.com (carried on Yahoo Finance, citing Bloomberg) and BigGo Finance; Yahoo Finance explainer for context
key_facts: Bloomberg reported on Friday 9 Oct 2026, citing people familiar with the matter, that OpenAI expects to reach or exceed $70 billion in annualized revenue by the end of 2026.
The growth is expected to be driven chiefly by OpenAI's enterprise business, the Bloomberg report said.
It came hours after the Financial Times reported OpenAI's annualized revenue was about $50 billion at the end of September, which sent the Nasdaq down 1.25% on Thursday.
Nvidia fell 2.9% and Micron 4.8% on Thursday; Nvidia and Micron rebounded in pre-market trading on Friday after the Bloomberg report.
Tech led Friday's recovery: the Nasdaq Composite closed up 0.64% and all three major indexes posted weekly gains.
OpenAI had not publicly reacted at the time of writing, according to Yahoo Finance; it is reportedly seeking at least $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation.
The MarketWatch original is not available here; its headline says chip stocks wobbled later in the day.
quote_evidence: OpenAI expects to reach or exceed $70 billion in annualized revenue by end-2026, Bloomberg reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter.
The growth is expected to be driven chiefly by its enterprise business, the Bloomberg report said.
The news sparked a pre-market rebound in Nvidia and Micron on Friday, and the tech sector ultimately became the core driver of the broader market recovery.
why_it_matters_hint: A second report eased the Thursday scare over OpenAI's revenue, which had hit chip and cloud shares.
